report:
**Yes — the evidence strongly supports that corticosteroids like dexamethasone improve survival in critically ill COVID-19 patients, though the benefit is specific to severe cases requiring respiratory support.**

## Key Evidence

**1. The RECOVERY Trial (NEJM, 2020)**
The landmark UK randomized trial assigned ~2,104 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to receive 6 mg of dexamethasone daily for up to 10 days, compared with usual care. Dexamethasone **reduced 28-day mortality by one-third in ventilated patients** (from 41% down to ~29%) and **by one-fifth in patients receiving oxygen only**. Crucially, there was **no benefit** among patients who did not require respiratory support, indicating the drug helps only the sickest patients.
Source: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436

**2. WHO REACT Meta-analysis (JAMA, 2020)**
The WHO Rapid Evidence Appraisal group pooled data from **7 randomized trials** and found that systemic corticosteroids were associated with **lower 28-day all-cause mortality** among critically ill COVID-19 patients compared with usual care or placebo.
Source: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279

**3. WHO Clinical Guidance (September 2020)**
Based on this evidence, the WHO issued a **strong recommendation** for systemic corticosteroids in patients with severe and critical COVID-19 (moderate certainty evidence), and recommended *against* their use in non-severe cases.
Source: https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-updates-clinical-care-guiduidance-with-corticosteroid-recommendations

**4. Ongoing Standard of Care**
Corticosteroids have remained the standard of care for severe-to-critical COVID-19 due to their effectiveness, accessibility, and low cost — particularly important for low- and middle-income countries.
Source: https://academic.oup.com/annalsats/article/20/4/596/8414890

## Bottom Line
The answer is **yes**, with an important nuance: dexamethasone and similar corticosteroids improve survival specifically in patients with severe or critical COVID-19 who require oxygen or mechanical ventilation. They do not benefit patients with mild disease and are not recommended for non-severe cases. The biological rationale is that severe COVID-19 involves dangerous hyperinflammation, which corticosteroids suppress.
